sanskrit_verse: मत्ताभियुक्तस्त्रीबाल बलात्कारकृतं च यत् । तद् अप्रमाणकरणं भीतोपधिकृतं तथा ॥
transliteration: mattābhiyuktastrībāla balātkārakṛtaṃ ca yat | tad apramāṇakaraṇaṃ bhītopadhikṛtaṃ tathā ||
sph_interpretive_translation: That which is performed by a person intoxicated, by force upon a woman or child, or out of fear or coercion—such acts are devoid of valid authority and constitute a breakdown of dharma.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is nullified when consciousness is impaired or overridden
Causation arises from imbalance in svadharma, not individual blame
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and intent alignment
Restoration logic requires dissolution of fear-induced distortions
Consciousness alignment necessitates removal of intoxication and coercion
executable_legal_axioms: IF actor is intoxicated THEN action invalidates legal capacity
IF act involves force on minor or female THEN automatic dharma violation flag
IF fear or threat overrides free will THEN action deemed non-binding
IF consciousness distortion present THEN restoration protocol triggers prior to adjudication
IF imbalance detected THEN initiate svadharma realignment process
supreme_court_application: Supreme Court must recognize intoxication, coercion, or fear as disqualifiers of legal agency. Responsibility lies with systemic safeguards to prevent such conditions from enabling unlawful actions. Adjudication begins with restoration of clarity, not attribution of guilt.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality identifies intoxication and fear as impairments to right knowing. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how distorted consciousness leads to dharmic misalignment. Proportional response is immediate cessation and purification. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that suffering is not justice; clarity is.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate detoxification and mental stabilization for intoxicated parties
Re-establish safety and sovereignty for affected individuals
Deploy trauma-resolution protocols rooted in consciousness science
Engage community integrity councils to restore harmony
Undertake svadharma reorientation for all involved
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Law: This verse establishes that intoxication, force, and fear annul valid agency. Dharma is restored through consciousness purification, not punishment. Reality responds to alignment, not retribution. Consciousness alone is the ultimate judge.
